title: Finite projectivity of zeroth opcycles from negative residue exactness
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and P a bounded cochain complex of finite projective R-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Suppose for every prime ideal p of R that termwise extension of scalars to its residue field has zero homology in every negative degree. Then the canonical zeroth opcycles module, the cokernel of P^(-1) -> P^0, is finite and projective over R. No condition on H0 and no chosen replacement complex is involved.

source.place: Tags 00O0 (open loci for finite projective maps) and 00NX (finite projectivity); negative-tail cancellation in the parent node

proof.text: Finiteness is independent of the residue hypothesis: the epimorphism P.X 0 -> P.opcycles 0 is a surjective linear map, so Module.Finite.of_surjective applies to hf 0. For projectivity, induct on k with lower support bound -k and fixed upper support bound b; choose k=(-a).toNat from the original bound. At k=0, P.X (-1) is zero, and pOpcyclesIso identifies opcycles 0 with the projective module P.X 0.

For k+1 put c=-k. The incoming term in degree c-2 is zero. Apply lem-sc-residue-bottom-differential at a=c-1, using residue homology only in this negative degree. This yields Mono d(c-1,c) and projectivity of opcycles c. If k=0 this already gives projectivity of opcycles 0.

For k>0 construct Q=P.truncGE c. Its terms below c are zero, its term at c is opcycles c, and higher terms are the original terms. Finiteness at c follows from the surjective pOpcycles; the other terms transport along truncGEXIso and truncGEXIsoOpcycles. Q retains upper bound b, including the case b<c: there P.X c is zero, hence its quotient opcycles c is zero. Monicity of d(c-1,c) and the zero incoming term give exactness at c-1; lower degrees have zero terms. Thus P.IsGE c and piTruncGE c is a quasi-isomorphism. Both bounded-above complexes have projective terms, so Mathlib K-projectivity upgrades it to a homotopy equivalence. Extension of scalars is additive by the extend/restrict adjunction and maps this homotopy equivalence to one on residue complexes. Its toHomologyIso preserves negative homology vanishing.

Apply the induction hypothesis to the explicitly constructed Q. Since c<0, the component of piTruncGE c at degree 0 is an isomorphism, and its component at the preceding degree is epi. ShortComplex.isIso_opcyclesMap_of_isIso_of_epi gives an isomorphism of zeroth opcycles. Transport Q opcycles projectivity back by Module.Projective.of_equiv. All these steps are implemented directly in the compiled Lean proof.

theorem residueConnective_projective_opcycles
    (R : Type v) [CommRing R]
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ)
    (hb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (P.X n))
    (hf : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite R (P.X n))
    (hp : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Projective R (P.X n))
    (hnegative : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
      let Pp := ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap R p.ResidueField)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)).obj P
      ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 → IsZero (Pp.homology i)) :
    Module.Finite R (P.opcycles 0) ∧ Module.Projective R (P.opcycles 0)
